A fat glow-worm laid in a hollow scooped into the moss pad, its cool gold rising up to warm the underside of each upright grass cord to amber, while a folded dock leaf arched over it keeps the glow from her eyes — one bead has rolled to the very lip of the hollow and stopped there.

A rose-hip with a twisted grass wick set behind the work, its red skin turning all the light ember-orange so the near row of pins glows copper and her knuckle goes rose-gold, one moth asleep on the rim with wings spread flat.

A stub of beeswax in a curl of birch bark propped shield-wise at the far side, throwing only a thin apricot stripe across the wet moss and the backs of her fingers, while a snail makes its slow crossing directly through the warm stripe.

A bead of amber warmed between her palms until it shines from inside, then set down in a crack with a broad sycamore leaf bent over it, gilding the near edge of the stone surface and one cold thumbnail gold.

A candle in a snail shell wedged into a knothole behind her, its aperture aimed at the work alone, laying a warm ivory pool along the row of pebbles on the stone and making the damp limestone go briefly gold.

Three glow-worms folded inside a dock leaf held under her chin, the green-gold seeping up to light the underside of her jaw and the stretched skin between her fingers while her eyes stay free above, a dewdrop on her wrist gone milky-warm.

A little pot of ember-moss with its lid slid half across, set down in a rain-pool hollow so the orange rises upward and stripes the hanging bead-cords from beneath in apricot, a beetle clinging to one cord directly in the warmth.

An ember carried in a walnut shell and blown on gently, the shell cupped in both hands so only the seam glows, that thin red-gold line falling across the moss pad and igniting the brass-pin heads in a row of tiny sparks.

A dish of oil burning one low flame sunk into a hollow in the bark, a curl of cork propped in front so only the overflow light reaches her, turning the nearest grass cords from teal to warm gold at every knot.

A bracket fungus on the trunk just behind her shoulders, glowing honey-warm entirely by itself, edging the full length of her outstretched arm in soft apricot and catching the highest bead on the cord in a bright point of amber.

A handful of luminous seeds cupped in one palm, fingers half-closed, the gaps between them leaking gold across the stone surface and making the row of pebbles cast tiny warm shadows toward her, one seed having rolled between two pebbles and lodged there.

A hollowed rose-hip with a floss wick, set low and behind the work so its red-filtered glow reaches only the near edge of the moss pad and the side of her jaw, a dry grass seed-head catching the ember-orange and going briefly copper.

A firefly in a walnut shell with a sycamore leaf bent over it as a hood, the gold leaking forward in a fan across the upright cords, warming them from silver-green to honeyed amber, a second firefly orbiting the outside of the shell.

A hot river pebble lifted from an earlier fire and wrapped in wet leaves, glowing at every split seam in deep rose-gold, set behind the work so only the seam-light streaks across the moss and the backs of three pinheads.

A curl of resinous pine bark with a grass wick burning in it, propped at a low angle so the flame faces the stone surface and away from her eyes, the pine resin making the light amber-green and the pebble row go gold on one side only.

A glow-worm on a twig laid across a hollow scooped into the bark, a broad petal folded over it, the diffused rose-gold coming up through the petal's veins and landing on her spread fingers and the near knot of grass cord in warm pink.

A bead of amber hung on a thorn and held close to the work, just behind the row of pins, so its inner glow touches each pin-head and the damp moss below them, her thumbnail gone translucent apricot where it rests against the amber.

A clay cup of ember-moss tipped onto its side in a root hollow, its open mouth aimed at the pad, the orange breath of it falling across the threads strung between pins and making each thread a fine line of ember-gold.

A firefly persuaded onto a twig stub wedged in a crack below the working surface, a half-walnut shell set over it as a dome with one edge propped up by a pebble, the escaping gold catching the underside of the moss pad green-gold.

A snail shell with a beeswax stub inside, set far to one side and half behind a root, its opening aimed sideways so only the edge of its ivory light reaches the cord and makes one hanging bead glow turquoise-warm on its near face.

A folded rose petal wrapped around a glow-worm and pinched into a cone, the magenta skin turning the light deep rose-red, held up under the work so the cords above are lit from below in warm crimson while her eyes stay cool above.

A split acorn cap with an ember of moss burning inside, its lid propped half over it by a thorn, the orange gap of it directed at the stone where the pebbles sit, making the wet pebbles shine in a row of amber mirrors.

A luminous seed pod split open and laid in the root fork below the working surface, its cold blue-green turning apricot where the resin inside has dried, the glow reaching the lowest hanging bead and stopping there, one hair-fine grass fibre catching it crosswise.

A wad of ember-moss in a cupped leaf held down at knee height, the leaf folded so only one edge lets the orange out, that stripe of warmth rising to catch the near face of each upright cord and leave the far face in violet cool.

A firefly in a hollowed elder berry, the deep-purple skin filtering the glow to rich rose, set in a crack below the moss pad, the rose light rising through the moss itself so the whole pad glows pink-orange from inside like a hot coal.
